source.title: Fixup Initialization: Residual Learning Without Normalization
source.authors: Hong-Yi Zhang; Y. Dauphin; Tengyu Ma

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests residual-network training without normalization using Fixup initialization, a different method from the claim’s shortcut and initialization examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 and ImageNet training outcomes relevant to training error. Its 10,000-layer depth result is first-epoch test accuracy, so it is not extracted as a training-error row. It does not report corrupted or random-label results.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests whether Fixup residual networks can train without normalization at BatchNorm's learning rate and convergence speed, bearing on the Fixup clauses of V3 and V6. It is an original source for both versions, so no verdict labels are assigned.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct, but proper regularization qualifies test performance, not the ability to match normalization in training. The authors conclude that Fixup enables reliable, fast residual-network training without normalization at standard learning rates; stronger regularization addresses overfitting and yields competitive test performance.
record.recipe_differences: Fixup rescales residual-branch initialization and adds scalar biases and multipliers; it tests residual networks without normalization rather than plain networks or the initialization recipes named in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale and bias parameters affect CIFAR-10 training: smaller scales slow learning, larger scales fail, and adding biases improves training. ImageNet Fixup without additional regularization overfits; Mixup is used to address this.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual-branch initialization scale affects training: smaller scales slow learning and larger scales cause failure; scalar biases improve training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In residual networks without normalization, architecture-dependent initialization scale and scalar biases determine training speed and stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixup Transformers train stably and as fast as LayerNorm baselines on machine translation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixup can replace layer normalization in Transformers while preserving training speed and stability.

record.problems: Training-error curves are figure-only and provide no stated numerical values or uncertainty. The CIFAR-10 training-accuracy plot covers only the first three epochs. The ImageNet training-error comparison uses curves reproduced from prior work for BatchNorm and GroupNorm.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports first-epoch test accuracy versus depth in Figure 3 and test-error or BLEU results in Tables 1–4; these do not measure training classification error and were left out.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero final training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 is not established by the supplied results. Random labels, corrupted labels, and the stated size and training-recipe qualifications are not tested.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of extra student neurons are not tested.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, longer-training controls, and very deep plain tanh networks are not tested.
The version concerns plain networks. This study tests initialization in residual networks, without plain-network activation-matching or orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons.
Initial stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability training are not measured.
The original sigmoid-MNIST, VGG-CIFAR-10, and Inception-ImageNet comparisons are not tested. The study tests the Fixup residual-network alternative.

missing.what: The authors explicitly report that CIFAR-10 ResNet-110 with Fixup uses the same learning rate and converges as fast as BatchNorm. They also report failure to train their Xavier-initialized comparator even at one tenth of that learning rate. These qualitative training results are not captured by the figure-only rows.
ImageNet training with Fixup is explicitly described as fast and stable with default hyperparameters for the ResNet-50 and ResNet-101 experiments; R3 captures only ResNet-50 training error.

record.verdict_notes: Fixup is an original source for V3 and V6, so labels are suppressed. Figure 3 and Tables 1–4 were already declared in rows_left_out. Figure 3's first-epoch test accuracy bears on V6's speed and learning-rate component, even though it cannot establish V1's near-zero training error. No numerical curve values are inferred from the text rendering.

versions.untested_parts: Corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-100, Adam, and comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes are not tested here.
Plain networks without shortcuts, longer-training comparisons for plain networks, and the cited alternative initialization methods are not tested here.
The paper tests Fixup as a way to train residual networks without normalization; it does not test all normalization speed and learning-rate claims in this version.

rows.note: The text describes a clear benefit from adding bias parameters and says smaller initialization slows learning while larger initialization fails; exact Fixup training accuracy is not stated.

rows.note: The figure compares BatchNorm with Fixup and ablations; no exact training accuracy values are stated.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Training error over 100 epochs with Fixup initialization and no additional regularization.
rows.measure: Training error; figure-only curve. Authors state Fixup fits the training data better and overfits significantly.
rows.baseline: BatchNorm and GroupNorm curves are shown for comparison; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The text explicitly says Fixup fits the training data better than the normalization methods and that this leads to overfitting; numerical training errors are not given.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports successful training without normalization and lower training error than normalization baselines. This supports the training-feasibility component; the row alone does not establish equal convergence speed or a depth comparison.

tranche.reason: Fixup changes initialization and auxiliary parameters to test normalization-free residual-network training and convergence relative to normalization.

source_check.notes: Exact curve values are unavailable; the explicit matched-convergence statement is in Section 4.2. Figure 5's BatchNorm and GroupNorm results are reproduced from Wu & He (2018).

statements.correction: Appendix C.1: smaller residual-branch initialization slows learning; larger initialization fails; scalar biases improve training. Section 4.2: default-hyperparameter ImageNet training is fast and stable; with additional strong regularization, reducing scalar-multiplier and bias learning rates by 10× is beneficial.
statements.problem: For this study's ImageNet recipe, reduced learning rates are described as beneficial for scalar biases and multipliers under strong regularization, rather than required generally.
